**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ABCB6 with a gain-of-function mechanism for either disease, or variants in different genes causing these phenotypes with no overlap in function, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs769248636)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of ABCB6 in mitochondrial porphyrin transport and eye development could reveal novel therapeutic targets for treating these rare ocular disorders.

Concurrently, these mutations impair erythrocyte membrane integrity, resulting in abnormal red blood cell morphology (MONDO:0014169).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ABCB6 with a consistent gain-of-function effect in both diseases, or complete segregation of mutations from the phenotype in affected families. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the dual role of ABCB6 in potassium homeostasis and erythrocyte membrane stability could inform therapeutic strategies for both hyperkalemia and rare red blood cell disorders.

#### 3. obsolete blood group, langereis system  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.657)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:47)

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ABCB6 in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies that target common molecular pathways for treating both conditions.

#### 4. X-linked sideroblastic anemia with ataxia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1369007)

Concurrently, impaired mitochondrial function can lead to neurological deficits such as ataxia.
